title: production-unwrap (Unwrapping Foreseeable Runtime Conditions)
damaged_code:
```rust
let conn = connect_to_db().unwrap(); // Crashes process if database is temporarily down!
```
pattern: Calling `.unwrap()` or `.expect()` on fallible I/O, network, database, or environmental lookups in a production path.
why_bad: Fragile, crash-prone architecture. These lookups rely on external systems that can easily fail in production (e.g., dropped packets, database server reboots, expired keys). Unwrapping these results turns a recoverable transient network hiccup into a full process crash. [15, Chapter 5]
detection: Calling `.unwrap()` or `.expect()` on `Result` types returned by standard library I/O, database drivers, or remote HTTP clients in a production codebase.
counterexample: Rust initialization doctests, unit tests, or main configuration parsing where a failure immediately at startup means the program cannot run anyway.
fix:
Handle the connection failure gracefully, returning a structured error.
```rust
let conn = connect_to_db()?;
```
source: *Jon Gjengset - Rust for Rustaceans*, Chapter 5, "Opaque Errors" [15]
